top_stories.title: 'Beer should be better in 2026': WC to boost global sales by a billion pints
top_stories.rephrased_article: A study by **Jefferies**, an investment bank, predicts that the 2026 FIFA World Cup will boost global beer consumption by one billion pints. The expanded tournament format with more matches and games in favorable time zones is expected to drive increased sales, particularly for companies like **Anheuser-Busch InBev** and **Heineken**.  The economic impact of the event, including tourism and GDP growth, is projected to be significant but may not have lasting effects.

top_stories.title: The World This Week | Nepal PM raises India border dispute, war in Lebanon casts shadow on US-Iran truce, Trump’s ‘new’ tariffs | UPSC Current Affairs News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: Nepal’s newly elected Prime Minister, Balendra Shah, reignited a long-standing border dispute with India by claiming that both countries have encroached on each other's territory.  Shah suggested reaching out to China and the United Kingdom for resolution, while India's foreign ministry spokesperson rejected third-party intervention. Meanwhile, US-Iran ceasefire talks stalled due to Israel’s ongoing campaign in Lebanon, leading to a heated exchange between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump. The US Trade Representative proposed imposing tariffs on 60 countries, including India, for failing to enforce prohibitions against forced labor.

top_stories.title: 7-Month-Old Palestinian Baby Killed After Israeli Troops Shoot At Family Car
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Israeli** troops shot and killed a seven-month-old Palestinian baby, Sam Fahd Abu Haikal, in Hebron's West Bank area on Friday after opening fire on his family car. The infant's father, Fahd Abu Haikal, claims the soldier who fired the shot saw him and his family clearly before firing.  The **IDF** stated that soldiers believed a vehicle was accelerating towards them and responded with single shots, injuring three Palestinians. The incident is under review, and the father demands accountability for the soldier involved.

top_stories.title: No Women In US Navy Promotion List Raises Fears Of Career Ceiling
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Pete Hegseth**, the **Defense Secretary**, intervened in a Navy promotion list, removing nine officers, including three women, from the ranks of one-star admirals. This action has raised concerns among female officers who fear their careers are being limited and that they face political bias within the military. The Pentagon has not provided an explanation for these removals, but Hegseth has previously argued against preferential treatment for women in the military, claiming it hinders combat readiness.  The Navy's promotion process has been transparent in the past, with a board of officers selecting candidates based on performance and qualifications.

top_stories.title: What Afghanistan’s rotten apples tell us about its non-profit sector | Poverty and Development | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: Funding for **non-profit** organizations in Afghanistan has dwindled, despite the growing need.  Projects often fail to address local challenges and are plagued by inefficiency, with reports of wasted funds and poor project outcomes. The situation is exacerbated by a lack of accountability and transparency among NGOs, as well as an extended chain of implementing partners that can lead to lower-quality work. This has resulted in missed opportunities to improve the lives of Afghans, particularly in rural areas.  The author argues for a shift towards employing qualified locals, avoiding complex supply chains, and prioritizing projects addressing pressing nationwide challenges.

top_stories.title: Israeli strike kills at least six people at wedding in Gaza | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: A **wedding** in Gaza City was targeted by Israeli forces, resulting in the deaths of at least six people and injuries to 15 others.  The attack occurred when projectiles struck a tent where a wedding was taking place, causing shrapnel damage and casualties. **Al Jazeera** reporters on the scene reported that women and children were among those injured, with the casualty toll expected to rise.

top_stories.title: Brother, Nephew Accused Of Killing NRI Over Property In Amritsar
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Amritsar Rural Police** have solved the murder of Australian NRI Sunil Sharma, revealing his brother **Satish Sharma** and accomplices conspired to usurp property worth Rs 5-6 crore.  The investigation, which began after a missing person report was filed on May 23rd, involved analyzing CCTV footage, phone data, and forensic evidence. The accused allegedly lured Sharma under the pretense of a property deal, sedated him, and struck him on the head before attempting to destroy evidence. **Satish Sharma**, his son **Sunny Sharma**, and property dealer **Lakhwinder Singh** have been arrested while two other suspects remain at large.

top_stories.title: Dubai police use AI to predict accident hotspots, detect speeding vehicles in real time - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Dubai Police** is utilizing advanced AI-powered traffic management systems to enhance road safety in the emirate. The system analyzes live traffic data, including vehicle volumes and speeds, to predict accident-prone locations and intervene before incidents escalate.  The force has also integrated AI platforms for real-time driver behavior monitoring and developed solutions for noise pollution identification. **Dubai Police** emphasizes technology alongside awareness campaigns to combat dangerous driving practices like hard shoulder overtaking. The force is also developing an AI system to automate minor traffic accident reports, aiming to streamline reporting procedures and reduce congestion.

top_stories.title: ‘Should we throw flowers?’: Videos show Khan Sir reacting to firing incident amid police search | Patna News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Faizal Khan**, also known as **Khan Sir**, a YouTuber and educator, is being sought by police after allegedly instructing his security guards to fire at a crowd outside his coaching institute.  Videos purportedly showing **Khan** commenting on the incident before students surfaced online, prompting police to appeal for calm and urge students not to be “misled”. Police are investigating the incident and have arrested two security guards employed by **Khan’s** institute over the firing. **Khan**’s lawyer has denied the allegations, claiming the FIR was lodged with a “retaliatory” intent.  Police are continuing efforts to trace **Khan** and have intensified security checks across the city.

top_stories.title: 'Where do you think I am from?' Indian-origin man counters racist bullying in Canada, says everyone should talk back - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: A video of an Indian-origin man, **Lovepreet Singh**, resisting a racist attack from a woman in Nova Scotia has gone viral. The woman, who was driving a car, asked Singh to go back to his home country and used derogatory language towards him.  Singh responded by calling her names and defending himself against the racism she displayed. He posted the video on Instagram, urging others to speak out against racism. While some social media users supported **Singh**, others questioned the context of the incident and expressed concern about the woman's behavior.
